text:
maria: Heads up — saw a flaky failure in the eval harness tied to the Next.js LlamaIndex starter. Looks like the Node SDK is returning embeddings in arrival order when requests are chunked/concurrent.
leo: can you paste the failing assertion and a short repro?
maria: failing test: `assert.deepEqual(received.map(r=>r.id), expectedIds)` — received order differs intermittently. Repro deck: send 8 small texts in one batch; sometimes order swaps.
arjun: which SDK + sample?
maria: samples/next-starter-llamaindex, using `@redwood/sdk@0.8.3` (Node). Python SDK (redwood==0.8.0) keeps input order.
kira: likely the JS batch implementation emits results as goroutines/Promises resolve. When chunking+parallelism >1, ordering isn't preserved.
leo: is this specific to embeddings.batch or also generation/streaming?
maria: observed in embeddings only so far; generation streams are fine because we map tokens back to request.
arjun: quick mitigation for the sample: add an `index` property to each item and then sort results by that index before asserting in the harness.
maria: I hacked a helper `reorderByIndex` in `api/embed.ts` and set `SAMPLE_EMBED_ORDER=stable` in `.env`. That fixed CI flakes.
kira: long term we should align SDK behavior: default preserve input order. Options: 1) SDK ensures stable order internally, 2) document that batch is unordered and provide helper, 3) add explicit flag like `batch({ preserveInputOrder: true })`.
leo: let's open an SDK issue and a sample PR. I'll create the issue and label it sdk/parity/regression.
leo: opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1024 — title: "JS embeddings.batch: unordered results when using parallel chunking"
devex-bot: issue #1024 created by leo — labels: sdk,bug,priority-high
arjun: I can prototype an SDK change: keep an array of placeholders and fill by index when responses arrive. Small perf hit but preserves determinism. We can gate that behind `preserveInputOrder=true` for now.
kira: also watch retry semantics: if a sub-chunk fails and retries, ensure dedupe by client-provided id. If retry returns both old and new we might get duplicates into the harness.
maria: good catch — I hit duplicates once when a transient 502 caused a partial retry. I added a dedupe step in the sample harness that reduces by id before scoring.
leo: assign @arjun to prototyping SDK patch, @kira to update eval harness tests to assert order+no-duplicates, @maria to submit sample PR documenting the workaround.
arjun: I'll target a small change in the JS SDK: preserveInputOrder opt (default: true). If tests pass we'll flip default explicitly later but keep compatibility note.
kira: for the eval harness I'll add a deterministic fixture and: 1) assert input order retained; 2) assert no duplicate ids; 3) run the test at higher concurrency to catch race.
maria: sample PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/998 — adds `reorderByIndex` helper and `.env` note. CI is failing on preview because eval-harness flagged ordering diffs.
devex-bot: preview deploy for pr/998 rolled back — reason: ci/tests:eval-harness failed
leo: good, failing CI is doing its job. Once SDK PR lands we'll remove the sample workaround.
arjun: drafting SDK PR to runtime branch, will include microbench numbers to show perf delta at high qps.
leo: please include a small migration note in the SDK changelog and a devex doc entry about "embedding batch ordering assumptions" so sample maintainers know to avoid brittle ordering tests.
maria: I'll add note to devex checklist and a short blurb in the Next.js starter README.
kira: closing loop: once SDK PR merges, update samples and disable SAMPLE_EMBED_ORDER env check. Also add an integration test to prevent regressions.
leo: thanks team — this turned up a subtle parity gap between Node/Python that we should avoid in future. :rocket:
